methods.label: Connect the inscribed angle to the tangent angle
methods.explanation:
Join the circle's center \(O\) to \(B\) and \(C\). These radii connect the angle at \(A\) to the angle between the tangents. Let \(d\) be the radian measure of \(\angle BDC\).

Since \(ABC\) is acute, \(0<x<\pi/2\). The arc \(BC\) not containing \(A\) therefore has central angle \(2x<\pi\), by the inscribed-angle theorem. Thus the smaller angle \(BOC\) is \(2x\).

A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at its point of contact, so the angles at \(B\) and \(C\) in quadrilateral \(OBDC\) are both \(\pi/2\). Its angle sum gives
\[
2x+d+\frac\pi2+\frac\pi2=2\pi,
\qquad d=\pi-2x.
\]
The given base angles of triangle \(ABC\) are each \(2d\), so
\[
x+4d=\pi.
\]
Substituting eliminates \(d\):
\[
x+4(\pi-2x)=\pi,
\qquad 7x=3\pi.
\]
This gives \(d=\pi/7\) and base angles \(2\pi/7\); all three angles of \(ABC\) are indeed acute. Therefore \(x=\boxed{3\pi/7}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

candidate.annotationRationale: The central targets are relating an inscribed angle to its intercepted central angle and using perpendicular tangent radii to determine the tangent angle. Triangle and quadrilateral angle sums supply the equations. The method works directly in radians, so radian measure is supporting knowledge; a separate degree-to-radian conversion procedure is not used. These assignments do not establish learner mastery.

review.mathematicalCheck: Acuteness ensures the intercepted central angle is the smaller angle BOC=2x. Perpendicular tangent radii and the quadrilateral angle sum give 2x+d=π. The triangle angle sum gives x+4d=π, so x=3π/7 and d=π/7. The resulting base angles 2π/7 are acute, and the configuration agrees with the figure.
